title: She Sang at the World Cup. Then She Walked Onto the TODAY Stage. Nora Fatehi Is Having the Summer of Her Life.
excerpt: From the FIFA Opening Ceremony in Toronto to Rockefeller Plaza in New York, the Canadian-Moroccan-Indian star just became the most Googled Bollywood artist on the planet — and she's only getting started.
body:
The stage at Rockefeller Plaza has hosted Taylor Swift. It's hosted Beyoncé, Ed Sheeran, Coldplay. On a July morning in New York City, it hosted **Nora Fatehi** — and she didn't just show up. She took over.

Performing *'Siir Siir'*, the official FIFA World Cup 2026 anthem, live on NBC's **TODAY** show alongside producer **Sanjoy** and French singer **Vegedream**, Fatehi delivered the kind of performance that makes you rewind and watch again. The energy was fierce, the choreography was razor-sharp, and the crowd at 30 Rock — not exactly known for losing their composure before 9 AM — was on its feet.

It was, by any measure, a milestone. **TODAY** is America's longest-running morning show, reaching millions of viewers every weekday. For a Bollywood artist to claim that stage — not as a curiosity, not as a cultural segment, but as a headlining musical act — is vanishingly rare. Nora didn't just get invited. She earned it.

## From Toronto to the World

The TODAY appearance caps a month that has turned Fatehi into something larger than any single industry can contain. On June 12, she performed at the **FIFA World Cup 2026 Opening Ceremony** at BMO Field in Toronto — the biggest stage in global sport. Hundreds of dancers moved behind her. The crowd roared. And by the time the lights went down, something had shifted.

Within days, Nora became the **most Googled Bollywood artist worldwide**, surpassing **Priyanka Chopra**, **Alia Bhatt**, and **Deepika Padukone** in global search volume according to Google Trends. Let that sink in. The woman who came to Mumbai a decade ago as an unknown dancer from Toronto just outpaced three of the biggest names in Indian cinema — not through a blockbuster release, but through a four-minute performance watched by billions.


![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)



> **""HISTORIC," she wrote on Instagram, where her 46 million followers watched her celebrate in real time."**



> "Canada gave me the base, Morocco gave me the roots, and India gave me the wings to fly."
> — Nora Fatehi

It's the kind of line that sounds rehearsed until you know the story. Born in Canada to Moroccan parents, Fatehi arrived in India with no connections, no family in the industry, and no formal training in acting. She taught herself to dance. She built her way up through special appearances in Telugu films — *Temper*, *Baahubali: The Beginning*, *Kick 2* — before Hindi cinema noticed what the south already knew: this woman was magnetic.

From *Dilbar* to *Saki Saki* to *Dance Meri Rani*, she turned item numbers into cultural events. And then she kept going.

## The World Cup Effect

The FIFA World Cup isn't just football. It's the single largest entertainment spectacle on earth, and the music programme is a career-defining slot. Nora first appeared at a FIFA ceremony during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. Four years later, she didn't just return — she co-headlined. 'Siir Siir' sits on the tournament's official album alongside artists from every continent. A significant portion of the song's music video crew — the choreographer, the dancers, the stylists — is Indian.

That detail matters. This isn't just Nora's moment. It's a signal that Indian creative talent is being pulled into the global entertainment machine at every level, not just in front of the camera.


![Ed Sheeran — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c1/Ed_Sheeran-6886_%28cropped%29.jpg)


Luxury watchmaker **Jacob & Co.** noticed too. The brand gifted Fatehi an exclusive, unreleased timepiece designed in the red and green of the Moroccan flag — a one-of-a-kind collector's piece that places her alongside **Cristiano Ronaldo**, **Lionel Messi**, **Rihanna**, **Jay-Z**, **Drake**, and **Salman Khan** in the brand's elite circle. You don't end up on that list by being famous in one country.

## The Diaspora's Biggest Export

And then there was the match. Morocco vs. Brazil, group stage, FIFA World Cup 2026. Nora was in the stands, draped in the Moroccan flag, singing the anthem, losing her mind when **Ismael Saibari** scored the equaliser against **Vinicius Jr.** to force a 1-1 draw. "HISTORIC," she wrote on Instagram, where her 46 million followers watched her celebrate in real time. "Our champions proved to the world that the Moroccan team is no joke!"

It was raw, joyful, unfiltered — exactly the energy that has always made her stand apart from the polished machinery of Bollywood PR. She doesn't perform fandom. She lives it.

For the Indian diaspora, Nora represents something specific and powerful: the possibility that you can belong to three cultures at once and let none of them go. She speaks Arabic at home, Hindi on set, French in music collaborations, and English on American television. She carries the Moroccan flag to a football match and then walks onto a New York stage to perform a song made with an Indian crew. The borders that are supposed to define an entertainment career don't seem to apply to her.

With *Siir Siir* still climbing playlists, a World Cup still in progress, and Hollywood now paying attention to the woman who just conquered its morning television, the question isn't what Nora Fatehi will do next. It's whether anyone else in Bollywood can keep up.

The summer belongs to her. She's not sharing it.
author: Diaspora Desk
